modern: One is a philosopher without a tunic, and another without a book: here is another, half naked: I have no bread, he says, and I hold fast to reason—and I do not get a living out of my learning, and I hold fast to my reason.
original: The one is a philosopher without a tunic, and the other without a book: here is another half naked: Bread I have not, he says, and I abide by reason—and I do not get the means of living out of my learning, and I abide [by my reason].
notification: One is a philosopher without a tunic, and another without a book: here is another, half naked…
notification_original: The one is a philosopher without a tunic, and the other without a book: here is another half naked…

explained.summary: One philosopher has no tunic, another no books, another is half-naked and has no bread, yet each holds fast to reason without earning a living from it. Marcus seems to admire them: wisdom doesn’t depend on possessions, and poverty needn’t shake your principles.
